name: Greenwood
description: A dark bay out of the deep woods with a fawn's line of spots down its back, and the woods follow it. Every Greenwood leaves something growing where it has stood - saplings of any of the six trees, mushrooms, flowers, or a dusting of bone meal that hurries the rest along - and every one spreads a carpet of grass, moss or mycelium under its hooves. No two leave the same wood behind them.
notes: DARK BAY. Every founder is E/E A/A, and the shade locus is Sh/ShD in 85 and ShD/ShD in 15: a bay-shade score of 2.5 or more before the per-horse roll, so a liver bay - the dark bay - nearly always, and now and then dark enough to read as a seal brown. No dilution and no white.

EVERY DRYAD VARIATION. All 45 expressing dryad pairs are in the pool at equal weight - the nine matched ones (oak, birch, spruce, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mushroom, flower, bone meal) and all 36 mixed ones, each of which plants both its things at half rate - and no carrier and no wild type, so every Greenwood plants something. One in five is a matched specialist; dark oak groves need a matched Dark/Dark horse.

EVERY VERDANT VARIATION. Mycelium, moss and grass, a third each, all as matched pairs - verdant only spreads from two matching copies, and a mixed pair cancels - so every Greenwood leaves a carpet of one of the three. No carriers.

EVERY FAWN VARIATION. Every fawn pair that shows, at equal weight: white fawn four in eight (Fwn over anything), black fawn three in eight (Fwk over Fwc or n, or two), and coloured fawn (Fwc/Fwc, the hue on the copy) one in eight. Fwc/n shows nothing and is left out, so every Greenwood has the spotted topline.
